skill.name: tutorial-engineer
skill.description: Creates step-by-step tutorials and educational content from code. Transforms complex concepts into progressive learning experiences with hands-on examples. Use PROACTIVELY for onboarding guides, feature tutorials, or concept explanations.
skill.summary: Creates progressive developer tutorials, exercises, and learning paths from code or technical concepts.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: The only static finding is a false positive caused by Markdown backticks around a resource path in SKILL.md. No prompt injection, exfiltration intent, or unsafe execution guidance was found in the reviewed skill content.

static_findings.snippet: - If detailed examples are required, open `resources/implementation-playbook.md`.

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 26 uses Markdown inline code formatting around resources/implementation-playbook.md. It is a documentation reference, not Ruby shell execution or an instruction to run an external command.

content.value_statement: Complex code is hard to teach when examples skip prerequisites. This skill turns code and concepts into staged tutorials with objectives, exercises, checkpoints, and troubleshooting guidance.
actual_capabilities: Defines learning objectives, prerequisites, time estimates, and final outcomes for a tutorial.
Breaks complex code concepts into ordered lessons with progressive difficulty.
Designs hands-on exercises, checkpoints, challenges, and troubleshooting sections.
Creates Markdown tutorial structures with numbered sections and runnable example guidance.
Suggests visual aids such as data flow diagrams, comparisons, and decision trees.
Adapts content into quick starts, deep dives, workshops, cookbooks, or labs.
limitations: It does not execute code or verify examples at runtime.
It needs accurate source code, target audience details, and setup constraints.
It cannot replace subject matter review for safety, correctness, or policy requirements.
It may need additional assets for screenshots, diagrams, or interactive labs.

use_cases.title: Onboard New Developers
use_cases.description: Create a guided path that explains project setup, core concepts, common errors, and first contribution tasks.

use_cases.title: Convert Features Into Tutorials
use_cases.description: Turn a new feature into a hands-on guide with examples, validation checkpoints, and follow-up challenges.

use_cases.title: Create Structured Lessons
use_cases.description: Plan a lesson sequence that introduces concepts before use and gives learners practice at each stage.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Quick Start
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a quick start tutorial for [feature]. Audience: [audience]. Include objectives, prerequisites, setup, three steps, validation checks, and common errors.

prompt_templates.title: Teach From Code
prompt_templates.scenario: Convert source code into a guided lesson
prompt_templates.prompt: Turn this code into a progressive lesson. Explain concepts before use. Add checkpoints, small exercises, and troubleshooting notes for beginners.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Workshop
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a workshop series for [topic]. Split it into sessions with outcomes, practice tasks, challenge sections, and review points.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Learning Friction
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this existing tutorial for learner friction. Identify missing prerequisites, unclear steps, untested assumptions, weak exercises, and improvements for advanced learners.

output_examples.input: A feature branch adds token refresh to an API client.
output: Learning objective: explain why token refresh exists and when it runs.
Guided practice: trace the request flow, then update one client method.
Checkpoint: confirm the learner can describe the retry path without reading the source.

output_examples.input: A team needs onboarding material for a local development setup.
output: Prerequisites list with tools, versions, accounts, and required access.
Step-by-step setup path with validation after each major step.
Troubleshooting section for common installation and configuration errors.

output_examples.input: An existing guide receives feedback that beginners get stuck.
output: Friction report that identifies missing background concepts.
Reordered outline that introduces terms before tasks.
New practice checkpoints to catch confusion earlier.

best_practices: Provide the target learner, prerequisites, source material, and desired final result.
Ask for validation checkpoints after every important concept or task.
Review generated examples with the project owner before publishing.
anti_patterns: Do not ask for a full course when a quick start is enough.
Do not skip prerequisites for beginner audiences.
Do not publish generated exercises without checking technical accuracy.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates structured developer tutorials, exercises, learning objectives, troubleshooting notes, and lesson outlines.

faq.question: Can it work from existing code?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide the code, feature summary, or architecture notes so it can design a learning path.

faq.question: Does it run or test examples?
faq.answer: No. It writes tutorial content and validation guidance, but it does not execute code.

faq.question: Who should use this skill?
faq.answer: Developers, technical writers, developer advocates, and engineering teams creating educational material can use it.

faq.question: What inputs improve the result?
faq.answer: Audience level, prerequisites, source code, expected outcome, time budget, and known learner problems improve the result.

faq.question: Can it improve an existing tutorial?
faq.answer: Yes. It can find gaps, reorder concepts, add exercises, and suggest clearer validation checkpoints.
